Appearance:

Shri Himanshu Paliwal, learned counsel for the appellan
 Shri Akshansh Mehra, learned counsel for the respondent

This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 30.06.2022 in MACC No.137/2019 by IInd MACT, Indore for enhancement of Rs.2,00,000/-.
2.

The Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,25,610/- in favour of the appellant/injured on the following heads:
Rs.5,04,000/-
Permanent disability (i.e Rs.6000+25% (FP)x12x14(M)x40/100 (PD)) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:1936 2 MA-5434-2022 Medical expenses Rs.1,89,610/-
Loss of income during Rs.12,000/-
 treatment  Pain & suffering Rs.10,000/-
 Attendant/special  Rs.10,000/-
 diet/conveyance  TOTAL 7,25,610/-

3. Appellant/claimant was awarded the said compensation for the injuries caused due to motor vehicle accident occurred on 21.08.2018 by negligent driving of respondent no.2, owned by respondent no.1 and insured by respondent no.3 which resulted in 40% permanent physical disability to the appellant/injured.

The appellant was 41 years of age at the time of accident and this appeal is preferred on the ground that income has been assessed on the lower side and compensation under the head of non pecuniary heads have not been adequately compensated.

4. Heard.
5.
Perused the record.
6. The tribunal has estimated the income of the appellant/injured as Rs.6,000/- per month whereas it ought to have been assessed at Rs.7,325/- per month.

In addition, the tribunal ought to have awarded compensation in the head of conveyance and special diet separately and for pain and suffering and loss of income during treatment is also insufficiently compensated.

Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is modified/recalculated as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:1936 3 MA-5434-2022 Rs.6,15,300/-
Permanent disability (i.e. Rs.7325+25% (FP)x12x14(M)x40/100 (PD)) Medical expenses Rs.1,89,610/-
 Attendant Rs.15,000/-
 Conveyance Rs.15,000/-
 Special diet Rs.10,000/-
 pain & suffering Rs.25,000/-
 loss of income during  Rs.21,975/- (i.e Rs.7325x3)
 treatment  Future treatment Rs.30,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.9,21,885/-
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.9,21,885/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.7,25,610/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,96,275/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,96,275/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
